subject: Archaeology
title: Baiae: Rome's Underwater Party Town
description: Learn Baiae: Rome's Underwater Party Town in one minute.

hook.text: Rome's most exclusive resort town is now underwater. You can snorkel over marble floors and villa walls.

buildup.text: Baiae was where Rome's elite went to party. Emperors, senators, and the wealthy built seaside villas with heated pools.

discovery.text: Volcanic activity in the Campi Flegrei area slowly lowered the coastline, sinking the town beneath the Bay of Naples.

twist.text: The ruins are so well preserved that mosaics, statues, and garden paths remain clearly visible beneath the waves.

climax.text: Baiae is now a marine protected area. Glass-bottom boat tours let visitors see Roman luxury beneath the waves.

punchline.text: Rome's playground for the rich is now a snorkeling site for tourists.

quiz.question: What caused the Roman resort town of Baiae to sink?
options: An earthquake collapsed the cliffs it was built on
Volcanic activity slowly lowered the coastline below sea level
Rising sea levels after the Roman Warm Period flooded the shore
